title: Base-change calculus and adjunction transport for integration transposes
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable] separated finite-type map of Noetherian schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ have Noetherian source. Form its Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ with $g':X'\to X$. Work in ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Write $F=Rf_!$, $F'=Rf'_!$, and choose their actual right adjoints $R,R'$ with units $\eta,\eta'$ and counits $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $C:g^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F'g'^*$ be the proper/open exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons].

Let $W\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $W'\in D(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $l:g'^*W\xrightarrow{\sim}W'$, and traces $t:FW\to A_Y$, $t':F'W'\to A_{Y'}$ satisfy $t'F'(l)C_W=g^*t$. Write $P_{f;K,M}:K\otimes_A^LFM\to F(f^*K\otimes_A^LM)$ for the canonical compact-support projection map, built from the proper projection map and the open-extension tensor comparison on a compactification [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection, lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], and similarly $P_{f'}$. Suppose the canonical projection maps for $W,W'$ are invertible on all inputs. For $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set $G_0K=f^*K\otimes W$ and $c_K=(1_K\otimes t)P_{f;K,W}^{-1}:FG_0K\to K$ (unitors understood). Define $G'_0,c'$ similarly, and let $\gamma_K:G_0K\to RK$ and $\gamma'_L:G'_0L\to R'L$ be their adjoint transposes [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Let $a_K:g'^*G_0K\xrightarrow{\sim}G'_0g^*K$ be the tensor/pullback comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] followed by $l$.

Let $e_K:g'^*RK\to R'g^*K$ be the transpose of $g^*\varepsilon_K\circ C_{RK}^{-1}$. Then
$$e_K\circ g'^*\gamma_K=\gamma'_{g^*K}\circ a_K.$$
If both gamma families are isomorphisms, $e_K$ is an isomorphism. Each gamma family is natural and uniquely determined by $\varepsilon_KF(\gamma_K)=c_K$. Whenever $\gamma:G_0\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ is a natural isomorphism, the transported adjunction $F\dashv G_0$ has exactly
$$\varepsilon_{0,K}=\varepsilon_KF(\gamma_K)=c_K,\qquad \eta_{0,M}=\gamma_{FM}^{-1}\eta_M,$$
and these maps satisfy both triangle identities. These statements impose no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor restriction.

proof.text: The coefficient-first compact projection is the composite of signed tensor symmetry, the existing natural transformation projectionMap, and direct image of signed tensor symmetry. Their naturality gives naturality in K and in W by composition of three squares. Invert the K-naturality square using hP, compose with tensoring t, and use right-unitor naturality. This proves naturality of integrationCounit. Apply Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_square to obtain naturality of integrationTranspose. The identity homEquiv.symm b = F.map b followed by the counit and Equiv.symm_apply_eq give unique counit normalization.

proof.text:
Write $H=g^*$ and $J=g'^*$, and let $\mu:H(K\otimes FW)\cong HK\otimes HFW$ be the inverse-image tensor identification. The compact projection/exchange square, with its canonical pullback-square comparison, followed by naturality of $P_{f'}$ in $l:JW\cong W'$, gives
$$F'(a_K)C_{G_0K}H(P_{f;K,W})=P_{f';HK,W'}(1_{HK}\otimes F'(l)C_W)\mu.$$
Here the exchange is exactly the proper/open exchange specified in the item, by its compactification normalization. All projection components in this equation are invertible by hypothesis. Compose with their inverses and with $1_{HK}\otimes t'$; the assumed identity $t'F'(l)C_W=H(t)$ and bifunctoriality of the tensor comparison yield
$$c'_{HK}F'(a_K)C_{G_0K}=H(c_K),\qquad c'_{HK}F'(a_K)=H(c_K)C_{G_0K}^{-1}.$$
The coefficient-unit identifications and unitors are those understood in the statement.

proof.text: Unfold integrationExceptionalExchange and integrationTranspose, and apply injectivity of the inverse Hom equivalence of the primed adjunction. Naturality of the inverse exchange at integrationTranspose moves F′ J(gamma) across C inverse. Functoriality and unique counit normalization then identify the resulting composite with C inverse followed by H(c). Step 2 identifies this with F′(a) followed by c′, proving the asserted transpose equality.

proof.text: If the two gamma families are isomorphisms, the equality just proved gives $e_K=\gamma'_{HK}a_K(J\gamma_K)^{-1}$. Every factor is invertible: $a_K$ is the prescribed tensor/pullback isomorphism followed by $l$, and a functor sends an inverse to an inverse. Thus $e_K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight on the actual adjunction and gamma.symm. Its counit component is F(gamma) followed by the original counit, and its unit component is the original unit followed by gamma inverse at F(M). The hypothesis identifying gamma.hom with integrationTransposeNatTrans and unique counit normalization identify the transported counit with integrationCounit.

Rewrite its unit with Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight_unit and its counit with the normalization from Step 5. These give precisely both displayed triangles on the actual maps, for arbitrary unbounded objects.
